notes.name: White Horde
notes.summary: The name ‘White Horde’ has conflicting meanings in historical sources and modern scholarship. Iranica associates it with Orda’s northeastern Jochid realm; Kawaguchi and Nagamine’s study argues that late-fourteenth-century Russian usage could denote the western wing or the whole Jochid ulus. A map label therefore cannot settle identity or an exact boundary. Consult the competing interpretations before comparing this area with the Blue or Golden Horde.

notes.name: Blue Horde
notes.summary: The color names of the Jochid wings are not consistent across source traditions. Kawaguchi and Nagamine identify late-fourteenth-century ‘Blue Horde’ usage with the eastern or left wing, while other historical conventions reverse the colors. This atlas’s label is retained for traceability, not accepted as a uniquely defined, settled-border nation. Compare the political organization, date and source vocabulary rather than matching color names alone.
